title: Medicine in the Waters
hook: the Vedas find medicine in the waters, so Hindu worship begins with water: sipped, sprinkled, offered
carry: water purifies: sip it, sprinkle it, offer it

segments.voice: Yesterday, the plants are mothers: spoken to as goddesses, and a tulsi watered every morning.

A glass of water on a nightstand. It's the first thing reached for in the morning and the last thing set down at night. Nobody calls it medicine. It just sits there, sweating a ring onto the wood. The Atharva Veda doesn't overlook it. In its first book, among the healing hymns, are verses spoken to the waters. Today is also the last day on the Vedas themselves, so after the waters, a look back.
screen: `A GLASS OF WATER ON A NIGHTSTAND.` → `NOBODY CALLS IT MEDICINE.` → `THE VEDA DOES.`

segments.voice: One verse, in paraphrase: you waters are the ones who bring us joy; help us to strength, so that we may see great delight. Another: within the waters is the deathless drink, within the waters is medicine. Another asks the divine waters to be kind to us, for our help and for our drinking. The word for medicine is bheshaja, the word inside the healer's all-healing hand. In these hymns the waters heal, delight, and are goddesses. That's why water stands at the start of so much Hindu worship. Before a puja, many sip a little water from the right palm three times, often with a name of Vishnu each time: achamana, cleansing from the inside. In the daily prayer called sandhya, these very verses, apo hi shtha, you waters are, are said while water is sprinkled over the head. Water is poured out to the rising sun, and many homes keep a small sealed pot of water from the Ganga, a few drops given to the sick or the dying. The teaching: water purifies, body and mind, and it's holy enough to begin anything sacred. And today closes the Vedas themselves: from the creation hymn and the cosmic person, through the Gayatri, Agni, Indra, Ushas, Varuna and the sung Sama Veda, down to a glass of water by a sickbed. Next, Ayurveda.
screen: `IN THE WATERS, MEDICINE.` · `ACHAMANA: THREE SIPS BEFORE WORSHIP.` · `APO HI SHTHA: WATER SPRINKLED.` · `THE VEDAS, FROM CREATION TO A SICKBED.`

segments.voice: If there's water near you, pour a little into your right palm. If you pray, sip it three times, the way many Hindus do before worship, with a name of God each time. If you don't, take one slow sip and follow it, cool on the lips, across the tongue, down the throat, and let it mark a fresh start.
The Atharva Veda's healing hymns. Hands, a cough sent flying, plants called mothers, and waters with medicine inside them.
screen: `THE ATHARVA VEDA'S HEALING HYMNS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: water purifies: sip it, sprinkle it, offer it. In the waters, medicine. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1285 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHERE DID AYURVEDA COME FROM?`
